title: How this book works
summary: Every rule has an address. Quote the address, not the page.
body:
Every rule has an address. Quote the address, not the page.

Numbers like 2.4 or A.3 are permanent. Page numbers move when the book grows; the address of a rule never does. "Follow 2.4" in a WhatsApp message to a printer is enough for them to find the exact rule, and enough for us to check the work against it.

One rule per spread. The rule, the reason for it, and the do and do not sit together on one page. Nothing is continued overleaf, so nothing is buried.

Three ways in: the contents on the next page, the find-it-fast index after it, and the A to Z at the back for anyone who does not know our vocabulary yet.

  • Do and do not. Always on the same page as the rule they belong to.

title: Where NEWGEN comes from
summary: NEWGEN Event Studio began in 2018 with one belief: a celebration should look, on the day, exactly the way it looked in the mind of the person who imagined it.
body:
NEWGEN Event Studio began in 2018 with one belief: a celebration should look, on the day, exactly the way it looked in the mind of the person who imagined it.

Mohan A started by sketching. Before a single flower was ordered or a stage built, he would sit with a family, listen to what they wanted their day to feel like, and draw it by hand, on paper, in front of them. That sketch became the promise, and the promise got kept.

Eight years later the same habit has carried NEWGEN through 1,500+ events and into three cities. The scale has changed. The sketch has not.

The name means what it says: next generation. It is built to carry NEWGEN through the next celebration, the next city and the next decade, and the descriptor "Event Studio" is designed to be removable when the hospitality chapter arrives.

"We sketch your celebration before we build it. What you see is exactly what your guests will feel."Brand promise. Locked, use verbatim.

title: Promise and tagline
summary: The brand promise and the tagline are locked. Use both verbatim in formal material. Never paraphrase, shorten or restyle them.
body:
The brand promise and the tagline are locked. Use both verbatim in formal material. Never paraphrase, shorten or restyle them.

Consistency is what makes them recognisable over time. A promise that is worded three different ways on three touchpoints is three promises, and none of them is remembered.

The tagline is set in Cormorant italic, with the calligraphic W. It sits beneath the descriptor, separated by the thin divider rule with its diamond centre point.

title: Personality, as evidence
summary: NEWGEN is premium, visionary and trustworthy. Each word is a claim, so each one is paired with something a guest, a venue or a printer can actually see.
body:
NEWGEN is premium, visionary and trustworthy. Each word is a claim, so each one is paired with something a guest, a venue or a printer can actually see.

Adjectives are cheap. Every decorator in Chennai calls itself premium. What separates NEWGEN is that each trait has a habit behind it, and the habit can be shown.

Premium

Not luxury, not budget. The tier where craft meets professionalism.

Seen in a gold Bering watch, a gold pen, a gold card holder. Nothing loud, consistent enough that a client notices the pattern without being told.
Visionary

Sees the event before it exists. Talks about what the guest will feel, not only what will be built.

Seen in the hand-drawn concept sketch that precedes every production order. What is approved on paper is what gets built.
Trustworthy

Says what will happen, then it happens. No vague promises, no unverifiable superlatives.

Seen in nine years with Sri Venkatesh Mahal, and the walkthrough checklist the crew follows whether or not Mohan is on site.
Never sound or look like cheap, generic, informal, "just another decorator", small-scale only. Test: if a line would sound the same coming from any competitor, rewrite it.

title: Three differentiators
summary: Three things set NEWGEN apart. Lead with them in that order, and let the first one carry the most weight.
body:
Three things set NEWGEN apart. Lead with them in that order, and let the first one carry the most weight.

These three are written once, here, and reused verbatim in the business profile, the website and every pitch. Do not invent a fourth for a particular document.

Sketch-led, not guess-led

Every event starts with a hand-drawn concept, not a mood board pulled from someone else's wedding. What you approve is what gets built. No surprises on the day.

Guest-first execution

The measure of a good event is not how it looks in photographs before the guests arrive, it is how it feels once they do. Every setup is built around the people standing in the room.

End-to-end, one team

Decor, AV, sound, photography, videography, logistics and catering coordination, all under NEWGEN, all accountable to one point of contact. No coordination gaps between vendors.

The Crown Pillar is the signature of NEWGEN. It is always reproduced from the master artwork, in one of the approved colours, and never altered.

The full mark is our signature: a temple pillar and flame finial woven into the N, where stability meets aspiration. Built to hold its presence with equal clarity across print, signage and digital touchpoints.

Chosen from 28 concepts with 80 percent public acceptance and the joint highest internal design score. It is designed to be the final mark, for twenty years, not two.

title: Approved lockups
summary: Six forms are approved. Choose by the space and by what sits behind, never by taste.
body:
Six forms are approved. Choose by the space and by what sits behind, never by taste.

Vertical lockup is the default: mark above NEWGEN above EVENT STUDIO. Vertical with tagline adds the divider rule and the tagline, for covers, signboards and the WhatsApp cover. Mark alone for square formats, watermarks and anything under the minimum. Wordmark alone only where the mark already appears elsewhere on the same piece.

The last two are container forms, and they exist for one reason: the logo sometimes needs to bring its own surface. The rounded card holds the full lockup. The solid mark is a disc with the mark cut out of it, and it is the form that survives being small or being stitched. Both are covered in 2.11.

A horizontal lockup is not part of the system. If a horizontal space forces one, raise it under 9.1 rather than improvising.

title: Never redraw
summary: The mark is only ever reproduced from the supplied artwork. It is never redrawn, retraced, retyped or rebuilt, by anyone, for any reason.

The mark is only ever reproduced from the supplied artwork. It is never redrawn, retraced, retyped or rebuilt, by anyone, for any reason.

A designer at a printer, a jersey supplier or a broadcast studio will offer to "recreate it in vector for you". The answer is no. The files already are vector. A redraw always drifts: the gap widens or closes, the flame fattens, the wordmark gets retyped in a lookalike face.

Send the files in 9.1. If a vendor cannot use them, that is a vendor problem, not an artwork problem.

title: Container forms: the card and the solid mark
summary: When the logo cannot trust what is behind it, it brings its own surface. Two forms do that job, and they are not interchangeable.
body:
Added 10 September 2026

When the logo cannot trust what is behind it, it brings its own surface. Two forms do that job, and they are not interchangeable.

The rounded card is the full lockup on a rounded rectangle. Use it where the logo needs a clean field of its own: a badge over a photograph, a sticker or label, a stamp on a document, a tile in a partner line-up. Corner radius is 12.8 percent of the short side and holds at every size. It is not the primary logo: on a letterhead, a signboard or a vehicle the plain lockup wins, because the card competes with the layout.

The solid mark is a filled disc with the Crown Pillar cut out of it. It carries no fine detail and no gap that a stitch or a die can close, which makes it the only form to send for embroidery, a lapel pin, a jersey patch, an app icon or a favicon. It holds at 10 mm in print and 32 px on screen, well below the lockup floor of 20 mm.

The solid mark comes in two builds and choosing wrong is the one way it fails. Knockout leaves the letter open, so the background shows through: use it only when you know what is behind. Two colour fills the letter, so it reads the same anywhere: send this one to anybody outside the studio.

title: Hierarchy and proportion
summary: Gold is used most. Teal second. Cream is the ground. Ochre is an accent only. Ruby is one small focal element per touchpoint, never a base colour. Black is never a dominant colour.
body:
Gold is used most. Teal second. Cream is the ground. Ochre is an accent only. Ruby is one small focal element per touchpoint, never a base colour. Black is never a dominant colour.

The proportion is the identity. Swap the weights and the piece stops looking like NEWGEN even with every colour correct.

The ruby rule is the one most often broken. One gem per touchpoint. If a layout wants a second red element, the first one loses.

No black as a dominant colour is Mohan's explicit call, not a stylistic preference. Treat it as a hard constraint in every review. Teal 100 does the work black would do.

title: Print notes
summary: Colour is approved on paper, under a fixed light, from a physical proof. Never from a screen and never from a vendor's PDF.
body:
Colour is approved on paper, under a fixed light, from a physical proof. Never from a screen and never from a vendor's PDF.

These notes travel with every print order. A printer who has read them has no reason to ask.

Physical proofAlways request a physical press proof for gold and ruby before final production. Approve proofs under 5000 K lighting.
StockUncoated premium stock wherever possible. Cream is never printed: the recommended stock is Crane Lettra 110 gsm Pearl White, or an equivalent warm white uncoated.
GoldPantone 871 C metallic for foil and spot. In process print, the dark shade #8B6200 prevents a flat yellow look on light backgrounds.
TealAvoid rich black overprints with teal. Use Teal 100 for solid dark areas. The 20 percent tint is essential for ghost patterns and watermarks on cream stock.
RubyMay shift orange-red on uncoated stock. Adjust to C15 M100 Y75 K10 if the proof shows it. Test before every new stock.
Coated versus uncoatedExpect gold and teal to shift on uncoated stock. Do not compensate on screen; compensate on the proof.

title: Two families, three roles
summary: Cormorant Garamond Bold carries the wordmark and every headline. Futura PT Light, widely tracked, carries the descriptor and every label. Cormorant italic carries the tagline and nothing else.
body:
Cormorant Garamond Bold carries the wordmark and every headline. Futura PT Light, widely tracked, carries the descriptor and every label. Cormorant italic carries the tagline and nothing else.

The contrast between the high-contrast serif and the pure geometric sans is the type system. It is intentional and must be preserved. Do not "fix" it by matching weights or by choosing a softer sans.

The display serif is never asked to carry small or dense text. Below 14 point, Futura takes over.

title: The kolam master tile
summary: One square tile, drawn as a single unbroken line. It repeats on a grid with zero spacing. It is never redrawn, only placed.
body:
Set the tile to the size the piece needs

One square tile, drawn as a single unbroken line. It repeats on a grid with zero spacing. It is never redrawn, only placed.

A kolam is drawn as one continuous line: the practice holds that an unbroken line keeps out what should stay out. Our tile keeps that rule. It is unicursal, and any version of it that breaks the line is not the pattern.

The tile and the single motif are two different assets and are not interchangeable. The tile is the ground. The motif, shown in 5.3, is the ornament that goes on top of it.

One tile, square, seamless on all four edges

title: Scale and placement
summary: The pattern is texture, not decoration. It sits behind, at the edge, or at a corner. It never competes with the mark and never fills a page at full strength.

The pattern is texture, not decoration. It sits behind, at the edge, or at a corner. It never competes with the mark and never fills a page at full strength.

Three proven scales. On a business card back it reads as delicate texture. On a letterhead band the geometry is visible. On an envelope lining the full pattern is legible and elegant.

The single motif, one tile standing alone, is the pattern's other voice: a corner mark on the quotation, a divider on a cover, an emboss on a folder.

Full-strength pattern behind text, the pattern rotated, or the tile scaled non-uniformly.

An unclosed kolam reads as "not yet complete". That is exactly the right picture for an empty category, a failed image, a 404 or an offline page, and it is completely ownable. Five compositions cover launch; the full library comes later.

Icons: one family, one stroke weight, one size scale. Gold or teal only, never multicolour. The line icon set on the right is the current family and must reconcile with the minimal teal icons on the business card back.

title: What a NEWGEN photograph is
summary: Real work, actually delivered, photographed with the hall as the subject. Warm, natural colour. Never stock, never illustrated, never generated.
body:
Real work, actually delivered, photographed with the hall as the subject. Warm, natural colour. Never stock, never illustrated, never generated.

The portfolio is evidence. A bride books from it, and on the day the room has to match the picture. Three approved moodboards set the register: Temple Heritage through a modern lens, Boutique Hotel Premium, and Sketch to Stage.

Photographs lead and copy supports. This is the one rule that makes the website and Instagram feel like NEWGEN rather than like a brochure.

title: The mandatory shots
summary: Five frames per event, minimum, in this order. A photographer who leaves without them is called back.
body:
Five frames per event, minimum, in this order. A photographer who leaves without them is called back.

The order follows the guest journey Mohan sells with: outside in, entrance to stage. A page built from these frames walks a visitor through the venue the way he walks a client.

FrameWhat it is
WideThe whole setup in one frame, from the guest's entry point. The establishing shot for every listing.
MidStage or backdrop, straight on, filling the frame. The one that sells.
Close-up, one or twoFlorals, the garland, the finish. Proof of craft, never a whole stage.
AtmosphereThe hall full, guests present, faces turned away or unidentifiable. The frame that shows it worked.
The sketchWhere one exists, the hand-drawn concept beside the built result. This is the differentiator made visible.
File by zone valet · lift placard · entrance and elevation · pathway · hall door · selfie point · welcome table · aisle · stage · hall · music and dance stage · buffet and dining · return gift point
tags: I am choosing photographs for the website or Instagram

title: Enhance, never regenerate
summary: Exposure, white balance, crop and noise may be corrected. Nothing may be added, removed or regenerated. A photograph that has been generatively altered is not a NEWGEN photograph.
body:
Grade action pending, see 0.4

Exposure, white balance, crop and noise may be corrected. Nothing may be added, removed or regenerated. A photograph that has been generatively altered is not a NEWGEN photograph.

The line is simple: a correction makes the picture truer to the room. A regeneration makes it a picture of a room that did not exist, and that becomes Mohan's problem on the wedding day.

NEWGEN records its own colour grade as a one-click action, values derived from the NEWGEN palette. Warm toward gold, shadows toward teal, 2 to 3 percent film grain. Never reuse another studio's grade: two Chennai decorators with one grade read as one gallery.

Before: as delivered from the phone
After: NEWGEN grade. Simulated here; the recorded action replaces this in v0.2
Do

Exposure, white balance, crop, straighten, noise reduction, dust removal.

Do not

Generative fill, object removal beyond dust, sky replacement, adding flowers, changing a colour of anything the client paid for.

title: People, faces and the photographer brief
summary: No identifiable guest faces without written consent. Crew and the founder may appear. Every hired photographer receives the one-page brief on this spread.
body:
No identifiable guest faces without written consent. Crew and the founder may appear. Every hired photographer receives the one-page brief on this spread.

Guests did not agree to be marketing. Shoot the hall, the setup and the atmosphere; turn faces away, shoot from behind, or crop. The bride and groom appear only with their consent, and then with pleasure.

Photographer brief · NEWGEN Event Studio
  1. Five frames minimum per event: wide from the guest entry, mid of the stage, one or two close-ups of the finish, the hall full with faces unidentifiable, and the sketch beside the result where one exists.
  2. Shoot the setup before guests, then again with the hall full. Both are needed.
  3. No identifiable guest faces. Crew and Mohan A are fine.
  4. Deliver RAW or highest-quality JPEG, uncropped, ungraded. NEWGEN applies its own grade.
  5. No filters, no AI enhancement, no generative edits of any kind.
  6. File names: venue, zone, date. Example: illam-priyam_stage_2026-08-14_01.jpg.
  7. Real flowers at muhurtham are the point. Get close enough to show they are real.
Artwork requests: eswar@eswarcreatives.in · NEWGEN Event Studio: +91 91760 45045

title: The voice in one line
summary: NEWGEN speaks the way Mohan works: it sketches before it sells, and it never oversells what it cannot deliver.
body:
NEWGEN speaks the way Mohan works: it sketches before it sells, and it never oversells what it cannot deliver.

If a sentence sounds like it is trying to impress, it is off-brand. If it sounds like a calm, capable person quietly showing you proof, it is on-brand.

If NEWGEN were a person: well-dressed, soft-spoken, carries a sketchbook everywhere, listens more than he talks, draws what you describe, and builds it exactly as promised. Bilingual naturally, moving between English and Tamil the way people actually do in Chennai. Write like that person is talking, never like a marketing department.

What clients should feel, in order
  1. Confident and assured. This team has done this before, at this scale, and it went right.
  2. Seen and understood. They listened to what was actually described.
  3. Moved, but only at the real payoff moments: the reveal, the finished sketch, the guest reaction.
"Nine years as Sri Venkatesh Mahal's decoration partner. Ask them why they never looked elsewhere."Show, then tell. Never tell alone.

title: Five principles
summary: Each principle is shown as a bad line and a good line, because the difference is easier to hear than to explain.
body:
Each principle is shown as a bad line and a good line, because the difference is easier to hear than to explain.

The good lines are real NEWGEN lines. Reuse them.

PrincipleOff-brandOn-brand
Show, then tell"We are Chennai's most trusted decorators.""Nine years as Sri Venkatesh Mahal's decoration partner. Ask them why they never looked elsewhere."
Specific beats superlative"Amazing weddings, unforgettable memories.""1,500+ events since 2018: weddings, corporate launches, and a few we are still asked to describe from memory."
Calm confidence, not salesmanship"Don't miss this chance to work with the BEST decorators in town!!!""We usually book out 3 to 4 months ahead. Worth a call before you lock your date."
The sketch is always the hero"Full-service event solutions for every occasion.""We sketch it first. What you approve is what your guests will see."
Warm, never over-familiar"Hi! We are SO excited to work with your beautiful venue!""A venue named with such devotion deserves work done with equal devotion."

title: Sentence mechanics and word choice
summary: No em dashes. No exclamation marks. No rhetorical questions in headlines. Never the word "unmistakably". Short declarative sentences. Numbers wherever a real number exists.
body:
No em dashes. No exclamation marks. No rhetorical questions in headlines. Never the word "unmistakably". Short declarative sentences. Numbers wherever a real number exists.

Use a comma, a colon, parentheses or a hyphen with spaces where an em dash would go. Avoid stacked adjectives: pick the one true word, or describe the detail instead.

Reach forsketch · vision · craft · precision · exclusive · proof · promise kept · team · system · process · accountable · guest experience · felt · remembered · Chennai, Tiruchi, Bengaluru · Illam, Aachi Masala, IC Mobile (named proof) · aha moment (Mohan's word for spyro, fog, flower shower)
Avoidmagical · dream come true · unforgettable · hustle · grind · one-man show · Instagrammable · viral · aesthetic as a noun · pan-India · top brands · leading companies · special effects (say aha moment) · ramp (say aisle) · 70 percent artificial (never in client copy)
Names, non-negotiableNEWGEN is always set in capitals in running text. Not Newgen, not NuGen, not newgen. Lowercase survives only where it is a technical convention: file names, the domain, and email addresses. The company is NEWGEN Event Studio, never "Event Makers". The founder is Mohan A, Founder & Creative Director, never "the CEO". The co-owner is MD ma'am in every client-facing line.

title: Register by audience
summary: One voice, six registers. Know who is reading before writing a word.
body:
One voice, six registers. Know who is reading before writing a word.

Three Tier 1 audiences share NEWGEN: HNI wedding families, mandapam owners, and hotel and resort GMs. Each gets a register, and the website has to hold all three on one homepage without feeling split.

AudienceRegister
Client WhatsApp, Mohan's own voiceTanglish. Domain words stay English (site visit, quotation, concept sketch), verb endings and connective tissue in colloquial Tamil, respectful plural (நீங்க) always. Written to be read aloud.
Mandapam owners, venues, hotel GMsThe most formal register. Short, sincere, low on adjectives. Credentials carry the persuasion. Never presume an existing relationship.
HNI and family clientsThe warmest register outside Mohan's own. Personal without being casual. Reassurance is the job, not excitement. Reference their vision specifically.
Corporate clientsThe driest register. Logistics competence and named proof first. No emotional language.
WhatsApp Business, automatedThe institutional voice: auto-replies, day 1, 3, 7 follow-ups, review requests. Warm, bilingual where useful, neutral enough to sound right from any team member.
Website, Instagram, LinkedIn, GoogleThe website carries the master tone, editorial and restrained. Instagram: short captions, the photograph is the pitch. LinkedIn: credentials, no wedding language. Google: factual, what happened, where.

Five caption shapes, one per channel. Copy the shape, change the facts.

Captions are short. The visual is the pitch; the caption is the caption. Avoid the industry openers: "Because every love story deserves..." and "Swipe to see the magic" are banned.

ChannelShapeExample

title: Glossary
summary: Twelve words a reader outside Chennai, or outside the trade, needs before the rest of the book makes sense.
body:
Twelve words a reader outside Chennai, or outside the trade, needs before the rest of the book makes sense.

Written for ISCL's design team in Bengaluru, for a printer who has never done a wedding, and for whoever joins NEWGEN next.

Aha momentMohan's own term for spyro, fog, flower shower, balloon release and palanquin entry. Never "special effects".
AisleThe walkway from entrance to stage, walked only by the couple. "Ramp" is the wider term and stays in search synonyms.
CrownThe flame and deepam at the top of the mark. Its height is the unit X.
DeepamA lamp. In the mark, the cap the flame rises from.
KolamA geometric pattern drawn daily at South Indian thresholds as one continuous line. Our brand pattern is a kolam.
MaalaiGarland. Not a bouquet: bouquets are the rows on a stage.
MandapamA wedding hall. "Mandapam setup" means the venue building setup, not the canopy.
MD ma'amThe co-owner of NEWGEN, always referred to this way in client-facing text.
MuhurthamThe wedding ceremony, and the canopy it happens under. "Muhurtham setup" is the canopy.
Sketch-firstNEWGEN's method: a hand-drawn concept approved by the client before anything is produced.
TanglishSpoken Chennai Tamil with English domain words, the register of Mohan's WhatsApp.
XThe unit every spacing rule is written in: the height of the crown.
